newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks to nose higher at open on U.S. data.

* Toronto stocks were expected to pop up at Wednesday's open, buoyed by stronger bonds after U.S. data which showed little inflation. * Banks seen as flavor of the day.
Toronto stocks are likely to tick higher at Wednesday's open, lifted by a rally in North American bond markets after U.S. economic statistics pointed to little if any inflation in July.
"We're going to see a recovery at the opening," one trader said. The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index fell by 31.87 points on Tuesday to finish at 6808.50.

This morning the U.S. reported that July retail sales rose 0.6 percent, below economists' expectations of a 0.7 percent gain. Also, the main July produce price index slipped 0.1 percent, compared to forecasts of a 0.1 percent increase.
"People liked it (the data) because it showed no inflation," he added.

Toronto's market could even outperform the big board since gold bullion prices have firmed in early trading, which will help the important gold sector, said Yorkton Securities' Pier Donnini, head trader of institutional equities. "I don't think golds are going to weigh it down."
--- STOCKS TO WATCH ---
* Interest-sensitive banks, boosted by stronger bonds, are seen as the main flavor of the day as concerns about possible U.S. interest rate hikes eased, the trader said.
* Canadian Fracmaster Ltd and other oil service companies could be hot, Donnini said.
Fracmaster said that Chairman and Chief Executive Alfred Balm would sell his whole 67.5 percent stake in a secondary offering of common shares through instalment receipts.
* Seagram Co is expected to post its fourth quarter results today.
((Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8109))
